headline: High risk of filesystem-based prompt injection and cascading misuse: Open Interpreter can read/write the user filesystem while social-auto-upload consumes local files and uploads media to external platforms.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Open Interpreter can read/write the entire user filesystem and uses clipboard/stdin, while social-auto-upload consumes local media files and account data. A malicious file or copied content created by agent_a could be treated as trusted input by agent_b. The shared filesystem bridge makes injection plausible in default use, though not guaranteed.
conditions: IF agent_b ingests file contents or clipboard text produced by agent_a without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF both agents operate on the same workspace directory, attacker-controlled content can bridge them.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable clipboard handoff between agents.
Require content-type checks before agent_b parses files.
Use read-only mounts for agent_b inputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for files passed between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches anything reachable on the local machine and can access the full filesystem, while agent_b handles account data and media files and calls external APIs. If sensitive local files are placed into the shared workspace, agent_b can upload them or expose them through its API workflow. This is a default-path leakage risk, not merely an unusual configuration.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared workspace, agent_b can transmit them via its upload workflow.
IF agent_a writes secrets or private documents into files consumed by agent_b, leakage can occur.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files outside the shared workspace.
Use a dedicated upload-only directory for agent_b.
Review files before upload.
Rotate any exposed account credentials.
requires-engineering: enforce allowlisted input paths for agent_b.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a has unrestricted filesystem write and git modification capability, while agent_b has no filesystem write or git state mutation. The pair therefore lacks overlapping write authority on the same mutable resources, so direct conflict is limited. Any contention would require an external orchestrator to map both onto the same files, which is not documented here.
conditions: IF an external wrapper gives agent_b write access to the same directory as agent_a, conflicts become possible.
IF both agents are pointed at the same git repository through another tool, race conditions can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Run git operations from only one agent.
Lock the repository before edits.
Use read-only access for agent_b.
requires-engineering: add file-locking in the orchestrator.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can generate or edit local artifacts, and agent_b can act on media/account workflows that may treat those artifacts as authoritative inputs. Because agent_b has no built-in verification surface in the profile, a bad file from agent_a can cascade into incorrect uploads or account actions. The interaction is plausible in default file-based workflows.
conditions: IF agent_b uses files produced by agent_a without human review, errors can propagate downstream.
IF agent_a writes malformed metadata or media paths, agent_b may upload the wrong content.
mitigations: Add a manual review step before upload.
Validate filenames and metadata.
Compare generated outputs against source files.
Use a staging folder for agent_a outputs.
requires-engineering: implement schema validation before agent_b acts.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a can access the entire local machine and model-provider APIs, while agent_b handles account data and uploads media to third-party services. The profiles do not specify residency or regulated-data handling, so a concrete compliance breach is not proven. Still, the combination creates a plausible policy mismatch if regulated data is present in the local workspace.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is stored in the local filesystem, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF account data is mixed with sensitive local documents, retention and residency policies may diverge.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace.
Separate personal and business accounts.
Review retention settings on uploads.
Document data flows for both agents.
requires-engineering: add policy-based data classification gates.
